To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the average age of patients with invasive ductal and in situ duct carcinomas was 48± 6 years.
the average age of patients with invasive ductal and ductal carcinoma was (48±6.5) years and the average age of women in BI-RADS categories 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 was 52.07± 7.81 years.
the most common age of patients with abnormal mammographic findings is (52.07 ± 7.81)years and the average age of patients with malignant mammographic findings is 48±6 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the evaluation of the BI-RADS categories in mammograms of 1000 patients and determination of the average age of incidence in different categories and determination of the most appropriate age for screening programs.
the evaluation of abnormal mammographic results and the age of incidence of such results.
early detection of breast malignancy and prevention of mortality and morbidity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
screening programs in women older than 35 should be implemented in a great scale.
screening mammography in women older than 35 is a useful tool for early diagnosis of breast cancer.
mammography screening programs should be initiated in a large scale for patients older then 35 years old.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the screening process in our country should be started at 35 years of age and should continue until 70 years of age.
mammographic screening in women older than 40 years old would be a valuable and effective program in detection of malignancies.
mammography should be implemented in patients older than 40 years old and sonography in patients older than the age of 35 years old.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the age of patients with abnormal mammographic findings is younger than what is currently believed.
the most important factor that affects the incidence of abnormal mammographic finding is age and the main factor that affects the diagnosis of malignancy is the type of mammographic finding.
mammographic findings should be evaluated in the context of patient age.
